2027-05-26.title: Second Wednesday of the Apostles
2027-05-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit
Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away
2027-05-26.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. In the Latin calendar today is the memorial of St Philip Neri.
2027-05-26.verse: Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and anyone who comes to me I will never drive away;
theo: This week the Gospel takes us back to the synagogue at Capernaum and to the long discourse on the bread of life in the sixth chapter of John. Over the coming days we will hear it piece by piece, and on Thursday, the Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ, we will hear its heart. Today Jesus speaks of those who come to him: “Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.” The promise is unconditional. There is no person so wounded, so sinful or so unimportant that Jesus would push them back from his door. He explains why: “for I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. And this is the will of him who sent me, that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me, but raise it up on the last day.” The Father's will is not a cold law; it is the will of a Father who does not want to lose a single child. Then come the murmurs: “Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How can he now say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?” The difficulty is familiarity. They know the carpenter's family, and so they cannot see the One who came from the Father. The evangelist uses the same word that the Bible uses for Israel's grumbling in the wilderness over the manna; these listeners, like the disciples a little later in the same chapter (John 6:60), stand where every believer sometimes stands, finding the words of Jesus hard. The danger is the same for us. We have known Jesus since our baptism, since the catechism class and the Sunday Qurbana of our childhood, and familiarity can hide him.

Jesus answers the grumbling with a word about grace: “No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father who sent me; and I will raise that person up on the last day.” Faith begins not with our cleverness but with the Father's drawing. That is good news for parents who pray for children who have drifted away, and for anyone who feels that faith is beyond them. The Father is already drawing; our part is not to resist. Four times in this chapter Jesus repeats the promise, “I will raise them up on the last day” (John 6:39, 40, 44, 54). The bread of life is not only for this life. It is a pledge of the resurrection of the body.

Paul's letter speaks of that same body. In Corinth some believers had a slogan: “All things are lawful for me.” Paul quotes it and corrects it twice: “but not all things are beneficial” and “but I will not be dominated by anything.” Christian liberty is not the right to be enslaved by appetite. The Corinthians thought that what one did with the body did not matter, since the body would perish anyway. Paul answers: “The body is meant not for fornication but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. And God raised the Lord and will also raise us by his power.” Because the body will rise, the body matters now. Then comes one of the great sentences of the New Testament: “Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God, and that you are not your own? For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.” Ten days ago, at Pentecost, we celebrated the coming of the Spirit on the apostles. In this Season of the Apostles Paul reminds us where the Spirit lives: in our bodies. That changes how we eat and drink, how we use our eyes on a screen at midnight, how we treat our own bodies and the bodies of others, how we care for the sick and the old, and how we lay our dead to rest. A temple is not something one abuses, rents out or neglects. It is something one keeps clean and fills with praise.
outline: Ask: do I believe that Jesus will never drive me away?
Point 1 · I will never drive away
The Father's will to lose no one; the murmurs of familiarity.
Faith as a gift, and the promise of the last day.
Point 3 · A temple of the Holy Spirit
Bought with a price: glorify God in your body.
live: If you have stayed away from the sacrament of Reconciliation, go this week: the Lord does not drive away anyone who comes.
Glorify God in your body (1 Corinthians 6:20)
Choose one concrete discipline this week for the sake of the temple: no screen after a fixed hour, no drink, or a daily walk with a prayer.
fathers: You are drawn not only by the will but by delight. Show a green branch to a sheep and you draw it; show nuts to a child and he runs to them. If earthly delights draw people, will not Christ draw us when the Father reveals him?

How can anyone say that the flesh is incapable of the gift of God, which is eternal life, when it is nourished by the Body and Blood of the Lord and is made a member of him? As the wheat falls into the earth and rises multiplied, so our bodies, fed by the Eucharist, will rise in their time.
magis: The human body shares in the dignity of the image of God; it is a human body precisely because it is animated by a spiritual soul, and it is destined to become, in the Body of Christ, a temple of the Spirit.
In expectation of the last day, the believer's body and soul already share in the dignity of belonging to Christ; this demands reverence for one's own body and for the bodies of others.
Chastity means the successful integration of sexuality within the person, and so the inner unity of the human being in body and spirit.
saints: Latin calendar: St Philip Neri (1515–1595), priest, the apostle of Rome, founder of the Congregation of the Oratory, remembered for his joy, his humour and his long hours in the confessional.

26–31 May: second and third weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Wed 26: in the Latin calendar, St Philip Neri. Thu 27: the Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ (the Latin Church in India keeps Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May). Sat 29: in the Latin calendar, St Paul VI. Sun 30: Third Sunday of the Apostles. Mon 31: the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which closes the month of Mary. The Sacred Heart of Jesus falls on Friday 4 June.
2027-05-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you came down from heaven to do the will of the Father, who wills that none of those he gives you should be lost. You never drive away anyone who comes to you. Draw us, and those we love who have wandered, into your company. Holy Spirit, you dwell in our bodies as in a temple: keep them pure and strong, make them instruments of praise and service, and raise them up with Christ on the last day. To the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit be glory for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lord who will raise us on the last day gives his own Body to our bodies. We receive him into the temple of the Spirit, and we go out bought with a price, to glorify God in the body he has fed.

quick: Jesus: anyone who comes to me I will never drive away; I will raise them up on the last day.
No one comes to Jesus unless the Father draws them: faith is a gift.
Paul: your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit; you were bought with a price, so glorify God in your body.
2027-05-26.action: Make one concrete choice today to honour your body as the Spirit's temple, and go to confession soon if you have stayed away.
2027-05-26.question: Have I let familiarity hide Jesus from me?

family.explain: Jesus says that he will never send away anyone who comes to him. Even when we have done something wrong, we can always go back to him. Saint Paul says our body is like a church where the Holy Spirit lives. That is why we take care of our bodies: we wash, we eat good food, we sleep, and we never hurt our own body or anyone else's.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick, old or disabled, and for those who care for their bodies with love.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way our family can take better care of the bodies God gave us?”

illus: A nurse from Kottayam worked in a care home in Ireland where many of the residents had no visitors. A younger colleague noticed how slowly and gently she washed and dressed the old people, especially the ones who could no longer speak. ‘Why do you take so much trouble?’ she asked. ‘Nobody is watching.’ The nurse said that her grandmother had washed her grandfather's body every day during his last illness and used to say, ‘This is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and one day it will rise.’ ‘So I am not just washing a body,’ she said. ‘I am cleaning a temple.’ Some weeks later the colleague asked if she could come with her to Sunday Mass.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you never drive away anyone who comes to you. We come to you now; draw us closer by your Father's love and fill us with your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away (John 6:37). When have I been afraid to come back to the Lord?
Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph? (John 6:42). Has familiarity made me deaf to Jesus?
No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father (John 6:44). For whom do I pray, that the Father may draw them?
Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19). How do I treat this temple?
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may welcome every person who comes, as Jesus does.
For young people tempted to treat their bodies as things to be used, that they may discover their dignity as temples of the Spirit.
For those who are slaves to drink, drugs or pornography, that they may find healing and strength.
For nurses, doctors and all who care for the sick and the old, that they may serve with reverence.
For our dead, that the Lord may raise them up on the last day.
pm.close: Father, you give to your Son all who come to him, and he loses none of them. Draw us by your grace, keep our bodies holy for your Spirit, and raise us with Christ on the last day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today Jesus makes a promise that we can hold on to all our lives: “anyone who comes to me I will never drive away” (John 6:37). No sin is too big and no person is too small. The door of Jesus is never shut to one who comes.

Why? Because Jesus came down from heaven to do the will of the Father, and the Father's will is that not one of those given to him should be lost. Jesus says it again and again: I will raise them up on the last day.

But some who heard him grumbled: is not this the son of Joseph? We know his family. They knew him too well to listen to him. We too have known Jesus since childhood. Let us ask for new ears, so that familiarity does not hide him from us.

Saint Paul speaks to Christians who thought the body did not matter. He says: your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit; you are not your own; you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body (1 Corinthians 6:19–20). The Spirit who came at Pentecost lives in us.

So let us take care of this temple. Let us keep it clean from what enslaves, use it to serve, care for the bodies of the sick and the old with reverence, and receive into it the Body of Christ, who will raise it up on the last day. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says he will never send away anyone who comes to him. You can always run to Jesus, even when you have done something wrong. And your body is like a little church where the Holy Spirit lives. So take care of it, and never hurt anyone else's body!

intro: Theme: “Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.”
The open door of Jesus, the Father who draws us, and the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit destined to rise.

points.h: Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away
sub: The Father's will to lose no one.
The door that is never shut.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and anyone who comes to me I will never drive away;
points.apply: Go to confession this week if you have stayed away, trusting the open door.

points.h: Drawn by the Father, raised on the last day
sub: The Father draws those we pray for.
The bread of life, pledge of the resurrection.
q: Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord God: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people; and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
This is indeed the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life; and I will raise them up on the last day.
points.apply: Name one person each day this week and ask the Father to draw them to his Son.

points.h: A temple of the Holy Spirit
sub: The body is for the Lord.
q: then the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and the man became a living being.
Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God, and that you are not your own?
points.apply: Choose one discipline this week that honours your body as the Spirit's temple.

concl: Jesus never drives away anyone who comes; the Father is drawing us and those we love.
The Spirit of Pentecost lives in our bodies: let us keep the temple holy until the Lord raises it on the last day.
2027-05-26.resolve: This week, come back to the Lord in confession if needed, pray daily for one person by name, and keep one discipline for the sake of the temple.
